A0053.title: PR Crisis Response
A0053.definition: When an organization faces negative public opinion, data-leak exposure, or a reputational crisis, PR, technical, legal, and customer-service teams coordinate disclosure, accountability responses, and remediation to contain escalation, reduce reputational damage, and restore public trust.
A0053.description:
PR crisis response is triggered when a security incident is publicly exposed or public opinion ferments. Its core is translating technical handling into externally understandable factual statements: confirming the incident's authenticity, scope, and measures taken in the first instance to avoid silence or denial triggering secondary fallout; synchronizing technical, legal, customer-service, and PR teams under a unified external voice, releasing tiered information through official announcements, media statements, and user notifications, and reporting to regulators within compliance deadlines.

Remediation includes offering remedies (e.g., free credit monitoring, password resets, compensation), setting up dedicated customer-service channels, cooperating with regulatory investigations and third-party forensics, and continuously monitoring social media and dark-web sentiment to clarify or document false information and malicious hype. It pairs with public-opinion monitoring (A0016) and reputational risk control as the external closure of security-incident handling (AC04).
A0053.limitation: Public opinion often ferments faster than internal incident triage and fact-checking; disclosing too early may leak investigation details or aid attackers, while disclosing too late is framed as a cover-up. Public sentiment and media interpretation are hard to fully control — even accurate statements can trigger secondary crises if remediation falls short of expectations. Competitors or illicit actors may inject disinformation to amplify reputational damage, and PR response alone cannot substitute for fixing the technical root cause; repeated incidents make trust recovery extremely difficult.
